claim_text: Direct HGB and direct Ridge achieve positive persistence-relative RMSE skill in all 119 station-horizon cells while collapsing forecast variance (alpha<0.5) in 118/119 cells each.
limitation: variance ratio diagnostic, ddof=0; two h=1 point-estimate exceptions (Huesca HGB 0.544, Barcelona Ridge 0.502)

claim_text: SARIMA reproduces the skill-with-collapse pattern: positive median RMSE skill (0.208) with collapse in 110/119 cells (92.4%).
Seasonal naive preserves variance (0/119 collapsed, median alpha approx 1.000) but has slightly negative median RMSE skill (-0.026).
limitation: naive reference, not a predictive model

claim_text: STL+Ridge preserves or inflates variance (median alpha 1.399) but has strongly negative median RMSE skill (-1.107) and is significantly worse than persistence in all cells under BH-adjusted DM.
limitation: control case; amplitude necessary but not sufficient

claim_text: Variance retention alpha(h)=Var(y_hat)/Var(y) is a post-evaluation diagnostic complementary to RMSE-based skill; positive RMSE skill can coexist with variance collapse (dynamic-fidelity loss).
limitation: diagnostic convention, not a formal loss criterion

claim_text: Skill_VP(h)=Skill(h)*alpha(h) is a bounded auxiliary that down-weights nominal RMSE skill under variance collapse.
limitation: reported as auxiliary, not a replacement metric

claim_text: No non-naive evaluated model attains any near-ideal cell (Skill>0 and alpha>=0.8): HGB, Ridge, SARIMA, STL+Ridge each 0/119.
The variance-collapse conclusion is robust to the alpha threshold (near-universal collapse for HGB/Ridge across alpha<0.4, <0.5, <0.6).
alpha is a variance ratio Var(y_hat)/Var(y), not a standard-deviation ratio; 14/14 audited cells match the variance ratio and 0/14 the SD ratio.
limitation: precision correction to the manuscript text; no reported number changed

claim_text: Positive persistence-relative RMSE skill can decouple from dynamic fidelity: skilful daily PM10 point forecasts can be dynamically over-smoothed.
limitation: interpretation of the joint skill-alpha pattern; not a causal claim
